subject.title: Allow before_agent_start hooks to override prompt

question: Should enabled prompt-mutating plugins be allowed to replace the current user prompt, and if so what precedence, transcript/audit, and cross-harness semantics are acceptable?
rationale: Current hooks deliberately expose additive prompt mutation behind an operator-controlled gate, but replacing the user’s input changes the plugin authority and needs an explicit durable contract before implementation.

options.title: Adopt a controlled replacement contract
options.body: Add an explicit `prompt` result to `before_prompt_build`, gated by existing prompt-injection policy, with documented first-wins precedence and equivalent PI, CLI, and Codex behavior.

options.title: Keep hooks additive and use blocking
options.body: Retain the current additive contract and direct plugins to `before_agent_run` blocking or context injection rather than allowing user-prompt rewriting.

recommendation.title: Adopt a controlled replacement contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit `prompt` result to `before_prompt_build`, gated by existing prompt-injection policy, with documented first-wins precedence and equivalent PI, CLI, and Codex behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared plugin hook type and merger are the central contract boundary for the decision.
